description:
Take It Slow Tonight | Slow Surbahar | 1.5 Hours

The day didn’t stop. It just finally ran out of things to demand from you.

This is for the hour between the last thing you did and the moment you actually rest. 90 minutes of slow Surbahar — long warm phrases, very low tempo, nothing sharp or urgent. Music that doesn’t ask anything of you.

The Surbahar has a deep, grounded tone — lower and heavier than a sitar. It doesn’t fill the room with brightness. It settles into it. Put it on and let the sound do what you can’t quite force yourself to do: slow down.

There’s space between the phrases. Silence that’s part of the music, not a gap in it. Your mind will keep moving for a while — that’s fine. The music is patient. It stays slow so you eventually catch up to it.

A quiet layer sits underneath at very low volume, gently guiding the mind toward a calmer state as the evening settles.

Good for the hour after work, winding down before bed, gentle stretches, or anyone who needs something steady to hold onto while the day finally lets go.

Press play. Let tonight be slow.

0:00 First phrases
15:00 Settling
35:00 Slowing down
60:00 Deep calm
80:00 At rest

If this helped you wind down, feel free to like, share, or subscribe for more daily music.

— Raga Focus

suno_prompt: Instrumental only, no vocals. Slow surbahar solo in raga Bageshri, late evening wind-down mood, deep warm plucked tones with long natural resonance and slow melodic phrases, no percussion, no tabla, 432Hz tuning, 45-55 BPM very slow tempo, sparse phrases with long natural silences between them, low-mid register (deep, grounded, not bright or high), cinematic healing production, settling and unwinding feel, suitable for extended looping. Raga Bageshri tonic C or D — late evening raga, intimate and calming. Emotionally: like the feeling of finally sitting down after a long day and realising you don’t have to do anything else. Patient, warm, unhurried. Theta wave layer at -20dB very subtle underneath.
